title: Third difference: why the aid is needed
source_text: LXXVI. Praeterea physicam praedeterminationem voluntati humanae ad bene operandum necessariam esse, ideo existimant Thomistae recentiores, quod voluntas, ut omnes reliquae causae secundae, opus habet a Deo causa prima praemoveri, ut actu operetur. Atque etiam illam necessitatem petunt a voluntatis indifferentia, quam propterea necesse sit a causa superiori ad agendum determinari. Sed Jansenius non alia de causa gratiae divinae auxilium efficax humanae voluntati necessarium putat, quam propter vulnus a peccato inflictum, & infirmitatem ex concupiscentia homini lapso adhaerente contractam.
pass_a_gloss: LXXVI. Further the more recent Thomists think that physical predetermination is necessary to the human will for working well, for this reason, that the will, like all the other second causes, needs to be premoved by God the first cause, that it may actually work. And also they seek that necessity from the indifference of the will, which therefore must be determined by a superior cause to acting. But Jansenius thinks the efficacious help of divine grace necessary to the human will for no other cause, than on account of the wound inflicted by sin, and the infirmity contracted from the concupiscence clinging to fallen man.
pass_b_english: Thesis LXXVI. Further, the recent Thomists hold that physical predetermination is necessary for the human will to act well because the will, like all other secondary causes, needs to be premoved by God, the First Cause, in order actually to act. They also derive this necessity from the will's indifference, which on that account must be determined to act by a higher cause.

Jansenius, however, thinks the efficacious aid of divine grace necessary to the human will for one reason only: the wound inflicted by sin, and the weakness contracted from the concupiscence that clings to fallen man.
